topics.label: Opening Framing
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the lecture topic and frames why complement is important despite its complex nomenclature.

topics.label: Fundamentals, Nomenclature, and the Central Role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the core architecture of the complement cascade, its historical naming rules, and the central function of C3 cleavage.

topics.label: Pathways of Complement Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three distinct upstream recognition routes—alternative, lectin, and classical—that converge on convertase formation and the activation threshold.

topics.label: Complement Effector Mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the three downstream actions triggered by complement activation: opsonization, inflammation, and membrane lysis.

topics.label: Host Regulation of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how regulatory proteins protect host cells from accidental complement-mediated destruction.

topics.label: Clinical Complement Deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses the diverse clinical manifestations and disease risks resulting from deficiencies in specific complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen Evasion of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes evolutionary strategies employed by microorganisms, notably Staphylococcus aureus, to evade or subvert complement defenses.

topics.label: Closing Framing
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the lecture and previews the upcoming topic on the adaptive immune system.
